title: EC2 Spot Instance Interruption Notices

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.29 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.29 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch:events` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" detail-type="EC2 Spot Instance Interruption Warning"
| table _time detail-type source detail.eventName
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.29_ec2_spot_instance_interr_29"
| sort -_time
description: Spot interruptions cause instance termination with short notice. Tracking enables graceful shutdown, workload migration, and capacity planning.
value: Detecting ec2 spot instance interruption notices early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Create EventBridge rule for EC2 Spot Instance Interruption Warning. Forward to SNS or Lambda for Splunk ingestion. Alert on every interruption; use for fleet metrics and hybrid/on-demand fallback decisions.
visualization: Table (instance, action, time), Timeline (interruptions by AZ), Bar chart (interruptions by instance type).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  where match(All_Changes.object, "(?i)spot|instance") OR match(All_Changes.app, "(?i)ec2")
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.action span=1h
| sort -count

knownFalsePositives: Intentional spot reclaim during game-day, batch jobs, and capacity tests where interruption is the design.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch:events`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `detail-type` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Create EventBridge rule for EC2 Spot Instance Interruption Warning. Forward to SNS or Lambda for Splunk ingestion. Alert on every interruption; use for fleet metrics and hybrid/on-demand fallback decisions.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" detail-type="EC2 Spot Instance Interruption Warning"
| table _time detail-type source detail.eventName
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.29_ec2_spot_instance_interr_29"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch:events` in `index=aws` to detect ec2 spot instance interruption notices. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `detail-type` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_29_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (instance, action, time), Timeline (interruptions by AZ), Bar chart (interruptions by instance type)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of ec2 spot instance interruption notices so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
